headline: Kept the $5.00 hourly rate for city EV chargers and approved widening the Pine Street sidewalk between Hall Street and Lowell Street.
summary: Officials also ordered speed and crosswalk studies for Warren Street, Trapelo Road, and South Street. Disabled parking spaces were approved at 31 Brigham Road and opposite 23 Elson Road, and a 5K road race on November 21, 2026 was recommended for a permit. The Wires Department was asked to repair five broken video detection systems after the Mayor denied $125,000 for the work.
decisions: Voted to wait for a new RRFB at Bacon Street and Plympton Street/Athletic Field Road, which the commission already approved.
Directed the Traffic Engineer to study whether a crosswalk should be added at Irving Street/Tomlin Street/Summit Street.
Directed the Traffic Engineer to conduct an RRFB warrant analysis for the South Street crosswalk between Hartwell Street and Angleside Road.
Directed the Traffic Engineer to conduct an RRFB warrant analysis for the Trapelo Road crosswalk at Briarwood Road.
Directed the Traffic Engineer to conduct a speed study on Warren Street between Beaver Street and the Watertown Line.
Approved the 15th Annual Piggy's 5K Road Race on November 21, 2026, and recommended a permit to the Mayor.
Approved a new disabled parking space at 31 Brigham Road.
Approved a new disabled parking space opposite 23 Elson Road.
Approved a conceptual plan to widen the Pine Street sidewalk between Hall Street and Lowell Street, with a 5-foot shoulder.
Directed the Traffic Engineer to have the thermoplastic contractor revise Adams Street pavement markings to 10-foot travel lanes and 7-foot parking lanes.
Voted to study Wadsworth Avenue and Fuller Street to see if pavement markings are warranted.
Directed the Traffic Engineer to review Moody Street at Spruce Street for an RRFB and estimate parking spaces that would be removed.
Directed Traffic Engineering to add pavement markings at Charles River Road and Angleside Road and asked the Forestry Division to clear vegetation blocking signs.
Directed the Traffic Engineer to add a four-hour parking limit and cross-hatch markings near the 25 Grant Street driveway.
Kept the $5.00 per hour rate for existing EV chargers, which will run only until October 28, 2028.
Directed the Traffic Engineer to replace the right-side STOP sign at Washington Avenue and Lowell Street and add a cross traffic warning sign.
Recommended that the Wires Department use its operating budget to repair five broken video detection systems.
Approved signal timing, detection, and walk-time updates at Lexington Street and Lake Street.

plain_text:
MINUTES OF THE TRAFFIC COMMISSION MEETING 
HELD: THURSDAY, OCTOBER 15, 2026, AT 10:00 A.M. 
WALTHAM CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER, CITY HALL 
 
The Chair made a motion, and the minutes of the September meeting were accepted. 
 
1. PETITIONED ITEMS:  
A. Bacon Street at Plympton Street/Athletic Field Road (Councillor LaFauci)       
Councillor LaFauci requested that the intersection of Bacon Street and Plympton Street/Athletic Field 
Road be converted to an All-Way STOP. Traffic Commission had previously approved the installation 
of an RRFB at this intersection. Traffic Engineering submitted a request for funding in May 2025, but 
the Mayor responded that the Wires Department will be responsible for the purchase and installation 
of the RRFB. The RRFB was never purchased and installed. The Wires Director, Mr. Kelly, stated 
he was not aware of this arrangement. He will review his budget to determine when he can complete 
the installation of the RRFB at this location. Voted to wait for the installation of a new RRFB, 
which has already been approved by Traffic Commission.  
 
B. New Crosswalk Crossing Summit Street (Councillor Durkee)         
Councillor Durkee requested the installation of a new crosswalk crossing Summit Street at Irving 
Street/Tomlin Street. Voted to direct the Traffic Engineer to study the intersection of Irving 
Street/Tomlin Street/Summit Street to see whether a crosswalk should be added on the 
eastley leg of the intersection, crossing Irving Street. 
 
C. Request for RRFB on South Street (Councillor Katz)          
Councillor Katz requested a new RRFB be installed for the crosswalk crossing South Street between 
Hartwell Street and Angleside Road. Voted to direct the Traffic Engineer to conduct an RRFB 
warrant analysis for the crosswalk crossing South Street between Hartwell Street and 
Angleside Road. 
 
D. Request for RRFB on Trapelo Road (Councillor Hanley)          
Councillor Hanley requested a new RRFB be installed for the crosswalk crossing Trapelo Road at 
Briarwood Road. Voted to direct the Traffic Engineer to conduct an RRFB warrant analysis for 
the crosswalk crossing Trapelo Road at Briarwood Road. 
 
E. Comprehensive Bay Colony Transportation Evaluation              
BXP submitted the transportation evaluation for the full Bay Colony conceptual development plan 
used in approving the zoning overlay district along Winter Street. The conceptual overlay shows the 
eventual development of approximately 1,100 residential units, as well as a fitness facility. Traffic 
Commission policy stipulates that for a zoning change proposal, a traffic study demonstrating the 
maximum traffic that could be generated from the maximum theoretical build-out of the development 
under the new zoning needs to be provided. This process was not followed. Last month’s vote 
included a requirement that for each subsequent phase of development, the traffic study should 
show the No Build condition that exists without any of the Phases constructed.  
 
Th overall Project is anticipated to generate 8,020 vehicle trips on a typical weekday with trip 
generation on Saturday being lower with 7,416 trips estimated. Peak hour is expected to range from 
611 to 706 additional vehicle trips. This is an addition to the traffic generated by those existing office 
buildings which will remain in place as part of the establishment of the MIRROD. Operationally, 
several key locations within the Winter Street and Totten Pond Road corridors are projected to 
experience continued congestion in future conditions even without the project, including locations
such as the Winter Street/Second Avenue/I-95 South ramps and the Totten Pond Road/Wyman 
Street/I95 north ramp intersection. For Information Only.  
   
F. Warren Street Traffic Calming            
A citizen petition was submitted for traffic calming measures on Warren Street between Beaver 
Street and the Watertown Line. Voted to direct the Traffic Engineer to conduct a speed study 
on the section of Warren Street between Beaver Street and the Watertown Line. 
  
G. 15 th Annual Piggy’s 5K Road Race, Saturday November 21, 2026      
Approval was requested for this road race .  Voted to approve this request and recommend to 
the Mayor a Permit to Issue. 
   
H. Proposed Disabled Parking Space, 31 Brigham Rd         
A disabled parking space was requested at 31 Brigham Road. Mark Johnson of the Disability 
Services Commission recommended approval. Voted to approve the request for a new disabled 
parking space at 31 Brigham Road. 
 
In Schedule 6 (Disabled Parking) of the Traffic Rules & Regulations, 
 
ADD: Brigham Road, east side, at #31 – 1 space  
 
I. Proposed Disabled Parking Space, 23 Elson Rd         
A disabled parking space was requested at 23 Elson Road. Mark Johnson of the Disability Services 
Commission recommended approval. Voted to approve the request for a new disabled parking 
space opposite 23 Elson Road.  
 
In Schedule 6 (Disabled Parking) of the Traffic Rules & Regulations, 
 
ADD: Elson Road, north side, opposite #23 – 1 space  
 
2. TABLED ITEMS: (Only items in Bold and Highlighted will be discussed at this meeting)
  
A. MBTA Better Bus Project Update (1/23) (1/24) (1/25) (1/26) (9/26)  
B. Traffic Signal Inventory: Winter Street/First Avenue (1/24)  
C. Traffic Signal Inventory: Winter Street/Second Avenue (1/24)  
D. RRFB Request, Moody Street at Adams Avenue (9/24) (9/25)  
E. Policy for Traffic Calming Requests (2/25) (3/25) (4/25)  
F. Wellington Street Speed Bump (Councillor Durkee) (4/25)  
G. West End Traffic Study Evaluation (Councillor Katz) (10/25) (11/25) (6/26)  
H. Parking Regulations on Private Ways (2/26) (4/26)  
I. Parking After Snowstorms (Councillor Harris) (3/26)  
 
J. Pine Street Vertical Posts (Councillor Logan) (9/26)   
Traffic Engineering recommended denying the request to install vertical posts along the south side 
of Pine Street between Hall Street and Lowell Street and instead recommended reconstructing the 
sidewalk along this block to be widened to 10.5 feet, including the width of the granite curb. This 
would reduce the shoulder width to 5 feet, which would still provide adequate bicycle 
accommodations, and for the occasional use by trash trucks, mail delivery vehicles, etc., but would 
still discourage parking. Voted to approve the conceptual plan to widen the sidewalk along the 
southerly side of Pine Street, between Hall Street and Lowell Street, to provide a 10.5 wide
sidewalk and a 5-foot wide shoulder. Traffic Engineering is to coordinate with Public Works, 
at any such time that Public Works is planning on repaving Pine Street.  
K. Traffic Signal Inventory: Newton Street/Pine Street Signal (Councillor Logan) (9/26)   
L. Traffic Signal Inventory: Moody Street/Crescent Street/Pine Street Signal (Councillor Logan) 
(9/26)  
M. Beaver Street RRFB (Councillors LeBlanc and Durkee) (9/26)   
 
N. Adams Street Parking Lanes (Councillor Harris) (9/26)   
On the section of Adams Street that was recently repaved from Maple Street to the southerly junction 
of Crescent Street, thermoplastic markings were applied to accommodate 11-foot travel lanes, and 
6-foot parking lanes on either side of the street. However, in the review of the pavement markings, 
vehicles were found to park partially into the travel lanes, due to the narrowness of the parking lane. 
The preferred dimensions should be 10-foot travel lanes and 7-foot parking lanes. Voted to direct 
the Traffic Engineer to assign the revision of pavement markings on Adams Street to the 
thermoplastic contractor, so 10-foot travel lanes and 7-foot parking lanes are provided. 
 
O. Wadsworth Avenue and Fuller Street Speed Studies (Councillor Harris) (9/26)   
The speed study on Wadsworth Avenue showed the 85th percentile was recorded to be 17 miles per 
hour. The 85th percentile speed on Fuller Street was recorded to be 18 miles per hour. Both streets 
demonstrate that speeds are well below the existing 25 mph speed limit. The Councillor asked if the 
review and potential implementation of pavement markings would help increase safety in the area. 
Voted to study Wadsworth Avenue and Fuller Street to see if the installation of pavement 
markings is warranted.   
 
P. RRFB Requests Along Moody Street (Councillor Dunn) (9/26)   
Traffic Engineering performed a pedestrian study along the stretch of Moody Street from Pine Street 
to Maple Street/High Street. The results show that pedestrians cross along all portions of Moody 
Street, whether they be at existing crosswalks or mid-block. In the area studied, 446 pedestrians 
crossed the street in a one-hour period. 62% of pedestrians used a crosswalk, while 38% of 
pedestrians crossed mid-block. Traffic Engineering recommended that no RRFBs be installed along 
this portion of Moody Street until the Moody Street redesign progresses. It was learned that this 
conceptual design is no longer moving forward. Despite this news, Traffic Engineering still did not 
recommend installing an RRFB at any location, as the nature of Moody Street promotes crossing at 
all points along the street. The 85 th percentile speed along this section of Moody Street is 
approximately 20 mph, and vehicles are frequently parking. Traffic tends to drive slowly, and 
pedestrian visibility is good. If Traffic Commission wished to install an RRFB despite the 
recommendation of Traffic Engineering, the most suitable location is on Moody Street at Spruce 
Street, since this location saw the greatest number of pedestrian crossings during the study (78 
total). Voted to direct the Traffic Engineer review this crossing to recommend the placement 
of the equipment for an RRFB at Moody Street/Spruce Street, should the Commission 
approve one, and estimate how many on-street parking spaces would be removed.  
 
Q. Angleside Road/Charles River Road Safety Review (Councillor Katz) (9/26)   
Upon review, Traffic Engineering concluded that the width of the intersection creates potential 
concerns because it is so large and open. Despite the fact that there have been no crashes at this 
intersection within the last three years, simple safety improvements can be made to make the right 
of way clearer to motorists via new pavement markings and better sign visibility. Traffic Engineering 
recommended the installation of new pavement markings to better define the intersection and to 
have the Forestry Division clear up the overgrown vegetation through the intersection to make street 
signage more visible. Voted to direct Traffic Engineering to apply new pavement markings at
the intersection of Charles River Road and Angleside Road, and to request the Forestry 
Division to clean up vegetation that obstructs traffic signs.  
 
R. Petition to Modify Parking on Grant Street (9/26)   
Residents of 25 Grant Street expressed difficulty turning out of the parking lot when large vehicles 
park in the designated on-street parking spaces. From Traffic Engineering’s review, there is available 
sight distance of approaching traffic from the right, as Grant Street is a one-way southbound. If a 
large truck were to park in the space just north of the driveway, sight distance is still available by 
looking behind the truck, or the vehicle can inch forward to increase the sight distance. However, 
there is no longer enough space for a vehicle to park just south of the driveway, with Traffic 
Commission’s new regulation of no parking within 2 feet of a driveway. Therefore, Traffic Engineering 
recommended installing an additional 4-hour parking sign to reinforce the existing regulation, while 
also painting cross-hatch markings in the space just to the south of the driveway to demonstrate that 
vehicles are no longer allowed to park there. Voted to direct the Traffic Engineer to install an 
additional four-hour maximum parking time limit just north of the 25 Grant Street driveway, 
and paint cross-hatch pavement markings in the space just south of the 25 Grant Street 
driveway.  
 
S. Car Charger Modifications (9/26)   
Traffic Engineering completed its review of the agreement with ChargePoint for the electric vehicle 
charging stations. The summary of what is included in the terms that have been agreed to are below: 
  
 19 EV chargers were purchased (through grant money) for $203,239 
 17 chargers are intended for municipal parking lots 
 1 charger is for the Library Lot and 1 charger is for the ice rink on Totten Pond Road (neither 
of these is under Traffic Commission jurisdiction) 
 Two subscriptions costs: one is a 3-year Enterprise Cloud Plan Subscription which covers 24/7 
driver support for charging sessions and ChargePoint accounts, etc.; one is a 3-year 
ChargePoint Assure Subscription which covers 24/7 proactive station monitoring, technical 
support, etc.; both subscriptions expire on October 28, 2028 
 the customer agrees to pay an hourly rate set by the City, plus applicable sales tax, plus a 
service fee to ChargePoint (typically 25 cents) 
 The city pays a 10% flex billing service fee to ChargePoint, equal to 10% of the net session 
fee  
 all revenue is collected by ChargePoint, with the City’s cut to be deposited on the 15 th of each 
month 
 
After looking at the total subscription cost of the 17 stations for 3 years, the City will need to 
accumulate $51,000, plus the cost of parking and the additional cost of electricity just to break even. 
Between the supply and delivery of electricity, the City is being charged 28.1 cents per kWh of 
electricity. Once you factor in the number of electric vehicle parking sessions over the course of the 
past month, it will be necessary to charge the customer $9.00/hr just to break even at the end of 3 
years. The City of Waltham is currently charging $5.00/hr to charge. The Traffic Engineer 
recommended that six months prior to the end of the ChargePoint Contract, which expires on 
October 28, 2028, that he be directed to work with Purchasing to put the purchase and installation 
of new EV chargers out to bid, in the anticipation of the termination of the existing chargers and 
subscriptions. Voted to maintain the $5.00 per hour rate for the use of the existing EV chargers. 
Establish that these chargers will only be in place and operational until the expiration of the 
current subscriptions (on October 28,2028). At least six months prior to the expiration of 
these subscriptions, direct the Traffic Engineer to work with the Purchasing Department to 
place the procurement of new EV chargers out to bid. Direct the Traffic Engineer to provide
all data to the Waltham Library Director and Director of Recreation, for the chargers in 
locations under jurisdiction of those departments. 
 
 
    
T. Washington Avenue at Lowell Street Interim Safety Measures (9/26)   
DPW is not able to reconstruct the ADA ramps at this time, and estimate that the work will be 
completed next year. In the meantime, Councillor Harris requested the use of a flashing Stop Sign 
in lieu of the existing stop sign. Traffic Engineering does not believe flashing red lights are necessary 
at this location, as it should be obvious that vehicles must stop. However, it may be less obvious to 
drivers that the traffic on Lowell Street does not have to stop at the intersection. Furthermore, the 
stop sign on the right is a little faded and has lost its retroreflectivity. Therefore, Traffic Engineering 
recommended replacing the stop sign on the right and installing a “Cross Traffic Does Not Stop” 
warning sign underneath it to warn motorists that vehicles on Lowell Street do not have to come to 
a stop at the intersection. Voted to direct the Traffic Engineer to replace the right-side STOP 
sign on Washington Avenue at Lowell Street, and install a warning sign to indicate that cross 
traffic does not stop. 
   
3. DEPARTMENT REPORTS:  
A. Parking Meter Report:   
Parking collections through the end of September totaled approximately $400,000. At the same time 
last year, parking collections were approximately $401,000, showing a roughly $1,000 decrease in 
parking revenue from this time last year.  
  
B. Traffic Commission Status Report:   
List of completed items: 
 Bus Stop at 41 High St 
 Embassy Parking Facility – two new stop signs installed 
 40 Clinton Street – Handicap parking space removed 
 Bay Colony Traffic Study advisory sent to City Council  
 
C. Update on Request for Funding for Traffic Detection (Five Signals)   
The Mayor denied the funding request of $125,000 (transfer from traffic mitigation funds) to fix and 
upgrade five intersections that are in need of video detection. According to the Mayor, this funding 
request was denied because she wants to see more progress with the Beaver Street Railroad 
Crossing project and the Main/Gore/Barbara/Warren project. Voted to suggest to the Wires 
Department to use its operating budget to repair broken video detection systems at 
Lexington/Wal-Lex/Brookway, Lexington/Ridge/Lionel, Lyman/Summer, Main/Willow, and 
Moody/Carter/Felton.  
 
D. Traffic Signal Inventory: Lexington Street/Lake Street   
 Traffic volume is down 
 Voted to update the signal timings, fix the detection, increase the minimum walk time and 
flashing don’t walk time, relocate Signal Head G on a taller pole, and update the phase 
numbers in the approved plan to match the phase numbers in the traffic controller  
 
AND ANY LATE FILED ITEM(S) THAT MAY COME BEFORE THE TRAFFIC COMMISSION. 
 
 
Adjourned @ 11:06 AM 
Attendance: All members present except Mr. Magno
Respectfully Submitted, 
Frank S. Lombardo, Clerk
